name: Vincent van Gogh
hook: Sunflowers, a severed ear, and a starry sky: the painter whose story Jeopardy tells in pieces.

facts.label: Starry Night
facts.statement: Starry Night (1889) was painted at the Saint-Rémy asylum, looking from his window at the town below.

facts.label: the severed ear
facts.statement: In 1888 van Gogh threatened Paul Gauguin, his roommate in Arles, and cut off part of his own ear.

facts.label: Sunflowers
facts.statement: Van Gogh painted Sunflowers in Arles in 1888, with the flowers in August bloom against a nearly monochromatic yellow background.

facts.label: Theo van Gogh
facts.statement: His brother Theo supported him; their letters, preserved by Theo's widow Jo, were published in English as Dear Theo. Vincent died in 1890 saying "The sadness will last forever."

facts.label: The Potato Eaters
facts.statement: The Potato Eaters shows a family gathered around a table dining on a plate of spuds, painted in 1885 before the bright Arles years.

facts.label: the Van Gogh Museum
facts.statement: The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam holds the world's largest collection of his work.

facts.label: Irises
facts.statement: Van Gogh painted Irises within his first week at the Saint-Rémy asylum, filling the canvas with violet-colored flowers.
